page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, this x86_64 instance provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The host features 16 GB of system RAM, yielding a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio typical of compute-focused configurations. Cache hierarchy includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 35 MB L3 cache per socket. Supported ISA extensions include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, FMA, AES, BMI2, and ADX. It contains no attached GPUs or local NVMe storage and offers a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth allocation.

Benchmark results show entry-level to moderate performance across various execution workloads. PassMark CPU tests yield an average overall CPU score of 6,992.04 and an extended instructions score of 6,075.96. However, single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests fall within the lower performance tier, paired with a Geekbench single-core score of 989 and a multi-core score of 3,785. Large-block uncached memory bandwidth reaches 40.27 GB/sec for reads and 35.09 GB/sec for writes, both in the average range, though cached small-block bandwidth remains lower. Lightweight LLM text generation using small 135M models runs at 116.97 tokens per second, but throughput drops to 5.21 tokens per second on 7B parameter models.

The ecs.c5.2xlarge provides a balanced hardware density for general compute tasks requiring dedicated Intel x86 execution without high local storage overhead. The absence of integrated NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached block storage, which relies on the 2 Gbps baseline network connection. Given its 1:2 memory ratio and modest single-thread execution efficiency, this instance is suited for batch processing, light compute jobs, web serving, and basic microservices rather than intensive database clusters or real-time AI workloads.

The instance includes no local ephemeral storage or integrated GPUs, depending instead on network storage and a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.
